steps.observation: You have 10 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action: A transformer reads a whole sequence at once. For every token it computes “self-attention”: scores that say how important every other token is to understanding this one. These scores weight and mix token representations, then feed simple feed-forward layers; stacking many of these layers lets the model learn complex relations. Positional encodings tell it where tokens sit, and (in language tasks) a decoder with masked attention produces the next token. It’s fast because attention is parallelizable, unlike RNNs that step through time.
